presets.label: 1. Data + UI + tool
presets.summary: One table, one query, one UI component and one agent tool, and what each becomes.

flow.note: typed fetch function the build writes for each query
SQLite/Turso, created from the table declaration
an agent calls the same function over JSON-RPC

notes.client: The build writes one typed fetch function per query or mutation. This is how a page reaches the server. React caching is optional: the build also writes `useVoxServerQuery(queryKey, queryFn)` in vox-tanstack-query.tsx, and you pass it a function like this one. (An earlier version of this page showed a hook called `useVoxQuery`. No such hook is generated.)
notes.ui: A `component` with a `view:` block (the Vox UI vocabulary: column, heading, text and so on) becomes an ordinary React component. This one only renders text. It does not call the query yet.
notes.mcp: A `tool` is exposed twice: as a function other code can call, and as an entry in the MCP server's `tools/list`. The description string becomes the tool description an agent reads.
notes.sql: The table declaration is the only place the schema is written. This statement runs when the generated server starts.
notes.rust: The server route for the query, the row type for the table, and the tool function, as emitted. This is excerpted output; it is not compiled with cargo on this page.

presets.label: 2. Result[T]
presets.summary: A query that can fail, and how the failure reaches the caller.

flow.note: arguments are sent as JSON query values

notes.client: The generated function returns `Promise<unknown>` today: the `Result` wrapper is not carried into the TypeScript type, so the caller has to check for `Ok` and `Err` in the JSON itself.
notes.ui: Another plain component. It shows static text.
notes.mcp: No `tool` in this file, so the build writes no MCP server.
notes.sql: The only table in the file.
notes.rust: The handler returns `{"Ok": value}` or `{"Err": message}`. Excerpted output; not compiled with cargo on this page.

presets.label: 3. Durable workflow
presets.summary: A workflow whose steps are recorded, so a crashed run can resume.

flow.note: each step is journaled by VoxDbTracker
set VOX_WORKFLOW_RUN_ID to resume a parked run

notes.client: Nothing is emitted: the file declares no query or mutation, so there is no browser client.
notes.ui: Nothing is emitted: the file declares no component.
notes.mcp: The `run_checkout` tool is the entry point an agent would use.
notes.sql: The table in this file. Workflow steps are journaled through the database layer as well.
notes.rust: The activity, and the workflow wrapper that opens a run, hands steps to the journal, and parks if the run does not complete. Excerpted output; not compiled with cargo on this page.

presets.label: 4. UI views
presets.summary: A component written in the Vox UI vocabulary (VUV): layout and text primitives, a typed button, and local state.

flow.note: local state becomes a React hook with the same type
event names are snake_case in Vox and camelCase in the output
one component used twice, with a typed argument

notes.runtime: This file declares components and no `main`, so `vox run` has nothing to execute. The component runs in the browser, as React.
notes.sql: No table in this file, so no SQL is emitted.
notes.rust: No query, mutation or tool in this file, so no server code is emitted.
notes.client: No query or mutation in this file, so no fetch client is emitted.
notes.ui: The VUV vocabulary replaces class strings and angle-bracket JSX. Each word (column, heading, text, button) maps to one HTML element and a fixed set of classes.
notes.mcp: No `tool` in this file, so there is no MCP server.
